claim: Hedgehog (Hh) morphogen is transported via vesicles along cytonemes emanating from signal-producing cells to form a gradient in Drosophila epithelia.
source: Previously we demonstrated that Hedgehog (Hh) morphogen is transported via vesicles along cytonemes emanating from signal-producing cells to form a gradient in Drosophila epithelia.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Cytonemes protruding from Hh-receiving cells contribute to Hh gradient formation.
source: Here, we demonstrate that cytonemes protruding from Hh-receiving cells contribute to Hh gradient formation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the manuscript supported by experimental data presented in the figures.

claim: The canonical Hh receptor Patched is localized in cytonemes from Hh-receiving cells.
source: The canonical Hh receptor Patched is localized in these cellular protrusions and Hh reception takes place in membrane contact sites between Hh-sending and Hh-receiving cytonemes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures, particularly Figure 2 and Figure 3.

claim: Hh reception takes place in membrane contact sites between Hh-sending and Hh-receiving cytonemes.
source: The canonical Hh receptor Patched is localized in these cellular protrusions and Hh reception takes place in membrane contact sites between Hh-sending and Hh-receiving cytonemes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data including GRASP experiments and colocalization studies shown in Figures 2-4.

claim: Hh-sending and Hh-receiving cytonemes have similar dynamics.
source: These two sets of cytonemes have similar dynamics and both fall in two different dynamic behaviours.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of cytoneme dynamics presented in Figure 1 and supplementary figures.

claim: Both Hh-sending and Hh-receiving cytonemes fall into two different dynamic behaviours.
source: These two sets of cytonemes have similar dynamics and both fall in two different dynamic behaviours.
evidence: This claim is supported by the classification of cytoneme dynamics into 'triangle' and 'trapezoid' models as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Hh co-receptor Interference hedgehog (Ihog) is critical for cell-cell cytoneme mediated interaction.
source: Furthermore, both the Hh co-receptor Interference hedgehog (Ihog) and the glypicans are critical for this cell-cell cytoneme mediated interaction.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of Ihog manipulation on cytoneme behavior and interactions, as shown in Figures 1, 7, and 8.

claim: Glypicans are critical for cell-cell cytoneme mediated interaction.
source: Furthermore, both the Hh co-receptor Interference hedgehog (Ihog) and the glypicans are critical for this cell-cell cytoneme mediated interaction.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of glypican manipulation on cytoneme behavior, as shown in Figure 7.

claim: Morphogens regulate tissue patterning through their distribution in concentration gradients.
source: Morphogens regulate tissue patterning through their distribution in concentration gradients.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge cited in the introduction.

claim: Specialized signalling filopodia, or cytonemes, play a role in morphogen dispersion and signalling.
source: Emerging research establishes a role for specialized signalling filopodia, or cytonemes, in morphogen dispersion and signalling.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to emerging research in the field.

claim: Morphogens are produced at a localized source and act at a distance, controlling the differential activation of target genes in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: During embryogenesis morphogens are produced at a localized source and act at a distance, controlling the differential activation of target genes in a concentration-dependent manner (Crick, 1970; Morgan, 1901; Rogers and Schier, 2011; Stumpf, 1966; Turing, 1952; Wolpert, 1969).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to foundational work in developmental biology.

claim: Active signal transport along specialized filopodia (cytonemes) is supported by increasing evidence.
source: Increasing evidence supports active signal transport along specialized filopodia (also called cytonemes) (Ramírez-Weber and Kornberg, 1999; Gradilla and Guerrero, 2013a, 2013b; Kornberg, 2014), challenging models based on the free diffusion of morphogens.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Active transport models for morphogen distribution challenge models based on free diffusion of morphogens.
source: Increasing evidence supports active signal transport along specialized filopodia (also called cytonemes) (Ramírez-Weber and Kornberg, 1999; Gradilla and Guerrero, 2013a, 2013b; Kornberg, 2014), challenging models based on the free diffusion of morphogens.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited evidence for active transport mechanisms.

claim: Hedgehog (Hh) morphogen has a central role in many metazoan developmental processes.
source: The Hedgehog (Hh) morphogen has a central role in many metazoan developmental processes.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field supported by citation.

claim: Hh is implicated in stem cell maintenance, axon guidance, cell migration and oncogenesis in a wide range of organisms.
source: Hh is implicated in stem cell maintenance, axon guidance, cell migration and oncogenesis in a wide range of organisms (Briscoe and Thérond, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Hh is post-translationally modified by the addition of cholesterol.
source: Hh is also post-translationally modified by the addition of cholesterol (Porter et al., 1996) and palmitic acid (Pepinsky et al., 1998), which promote its association with cell membranes making Hh transport potentially inconsistent with free morphogen diffusion.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Porter et al., 1996.

claim: Hh is post-translationally modified by the addition of palmitic acid.
source: Hh is also post-translationally modified by the addition of cholesterol (Porter et al., 1996) and palmitic acid (Pepinsky et al., 1998), which promote its association with cell membranes making Hh transport potentially inconsistent with free morphogen diffusion.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Pepinsky et al., 1998.

claim: Cholesterol and palmitic acid modifications promote Hh association with cell membranes.
source: Hh is also post-translationally modified by the addition of cholesterol (Porter et al., 1996) and palmitic acid (Pepinsky et al., 1998), which promote its association with cell membranes making Hh transport potentially inconsistent with free morphogen diffusion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited studies about lipid modifications.

claim: Lipid modifications of Hh make its transport potentially inconsistent with free morphogen diffusion.
source: Hh is also post-translationally modified by the addition of cholesterol (Porter et al., 1996) and palmitic acid (Pepinsky et al., 1998), which promote its association with cell membranes making Hh transport potentially inconsistent with free morphogen diffusion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the physical properties of lipid-modified proteins.

claim: Hh gradient establishment has been extensively studied in the Drosophila wing imaginal disc epithelium.
source: Hh gradient establishment has been extensively studied in the Drosophila wing imaginal disc epithelium, which is formed by anterior (A) and posterior (P) cell populations with different adhesion affinities.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: The Drosophila wing imaginal disc epithelium is formed by anterior (A) and posterior (P) cell populations with different adhesion affinities.
source: Hh gradient establishment has been extensively studied in the Drosophila wing imaginal disc epithelium, which is formed by anterior (A) and posterior (P) cell populations with different adhesion affinities.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila wing disc development.

claim: The P compartment cells produce Hh, which moves across the A/P compartment border to reach the Hh-responding cells in the A compartment.
source: The P compartment cells produce Hh, which moves across the A/P compartment border to reach the Hh-responding cells in the A compartment.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Hh signaling in the wing disc.

claim: As Hh spreads away from the A/P border, its concentration decreases, providing a graded signal that activates different target genes.
source: As Hh spreads away from the border, its concentration decreases, providing a graded signal that activates the different target genes that regulate imaginal disc development (reviewed in Briscoe and Thérond, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to a review.

claim: Cytonemes from Hh-producing cells extend across the Hh morphogenetic gradient in both wing disc and abdominal histoblasts.
source: In both wing disc and abdominal histoblasts, cytonemes from Hh-producing cells extend across its morphogenetic gradient (Bischoff et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: There is a strong correlation between the extent of cytonemes from the P compartment and the graded response to Hh signalling in the A compartment.
source: Critically, there is a strong correlation between the extent of cytonemes from the P compartment and the graded response to Hh signalling in the A compartment.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Bischoff et al., 2013).

claim: In vivo imaging of abdominal histoblasts showed that cytonemes extend and retract dynamically.
source: In vivo imaging of abdominal histoblasts showed that cytonemes extend and retract dynamically, and that Hh gradient establishment correlates with cytoneme formation in both space and time.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Hh gradient establishment correlates with cytoneme formation in both space and time.
source: In vivo imaging of abdominal histoblasts showed that cytonemes extend and retract dynamically, and that Hh gradient establishment correlates with cytoneme formation in both space and time.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Cytonemes act as conduits for Hh movement mainly at the basal plane of the epithelium.
source: These data support a model for Hh transport in which cytonemes act as conduits for morphogen movement mainly at the basal plane of the epithelium.
evidence: This is an inference based on cited previous work.

claim: Hh is associated with vesicles transported along cytonemes.
source: Furthermore, we have shown that Hh is associated with vesicles transported along cytonemes (Gradilla et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Hh-receiving cells in the A compartment extend cytonemes towards the Hh-secreting cells of the P compartment.
source: In addition, the Hh-receiving cells of the anterior compartment also extend cytonemes towards the Hh-secreting cells of the P compartment.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Hh-receiving cells produce highly dynamic protrusions oriented towards the Hh-producing cells.
source: The Hh-receiving cells also produce highly dynamic protrusions oriented towards the Hh-producing cells, easily visualized when expressing the actin-binding domain of moesin (GMA) fused to GFP (Figure 1A, Video 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and Video 1A.

claim: GMA-labelled filopodia are less dynamic when they co-express Ihog.
source: These GMA-labelled filopodia are less dynamic when they co-express Ihog (Figure 1B, Video 1B), as was previously described for the Hh-producing histoblasts (Bischoff et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and Video 1B, and by citation to previous work.

claim: Both Hh-presenting and Hh-receiving histoblast cells emit protrusions with similar dynamics.
source: Here we show that both Hh-presenting and Hh-receiving histoblast cells emit protrusions with similar dynamics (Video 1 and Video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Videos 1 and 2.

claim: Filopodia can be classified into two different dynamic behaviours: 'triangle dynamics' and 'trapezoid dynamics'.
source: In a more detailed analysis of filopodia dynamics, we have been able to distinguish two different dynamic behaviours: one of filopodia that elongate and immediately retract, which we have classified as 'triangle dynamics' and another one with a 'stationary' interphase between the elongation and retraction phases, which we have classified as 'trapezoid dynamics' (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; see Materials and methods).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and described in Materials and methods.

claim: Both Hh-producing and Hh-receiving cell filopodia have similar values of average maximum extent, lifetime, elongation (Ve) and retraction (Vr) velocities.
source: Both Hh-producing and Hh-receiving cell filopodia have similar values of average maximum extent, lifetime, elongation (Ve) and retraction (Vr) velocities (Figure 1C–E, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data presented in Figure 1C-E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The maximum extent of filopodia is similar with or without overexpression of Ihog.
source: The maximum extent of filopodia is similar with or without overexpression of Ihog (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ihog overexpression changes cytoneme dynamics.
source: This overexpression, however, changes cytoneme dynamics.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Filopodia lifetime values are higher for filopodia with high levels of Ihog than those with low levels.
source: Filopodia lifetime values are higher for filopodia with high levels of Ihog than those with low levels (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Hh-producing and Hh-receiving cell filopodia elongate and retract at similar rates.
source: Hh-producing and Hh-receiving cell filopodia elongate and retract at similar rates (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Ihog overexpression leads to more stable cytonemes in the A compartment cells.
source: In summary, Ihog overexpression leads to more stable cytonemes also in the A compartment cells.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Knocking down SCAR, Diaphanous (Dia), Filamin (Cheerio, Cher) or actin Capping protein alpha (Cpa) in the A compartment results in reduced Ptc and Ci expression domains.
source: We knocked down SCAR, Diaphanous (Dia), Filamin (Cheerio, Cher) or actin Capping protein alpha (Cpa) function in the A compartment using specific RNAi lines. In addition, we expressed these RNAis together with ihog-RFP to visualize cytonemes. The aberrant extension of cytonemes observed by knocking down these proteins in the Hh-receiving cells resulted in reduced Ptc and Ci expression domains (Figure 1F), revealing a role of the A compartment cytonemes in regulating the Hh gradient.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1F.

claim: A compartment cytonemes have a role in regulating the Hh gradient.
source: The aberrant extension of cytonemes observed by knocking down these proteins in the Hh-receiving cells resulted in reduced Ptc and Ci expression domains (Figure 1F), revealing a role of the A compartment cytonemes in regulating the Hh gradient.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing effects of cytoneme manipulation on Hh signaling.

claim: Cytonemes control both Hh export from P compartment and Hh distribution and reception in the A compartment.
source: Thus, cytonemes control both Hh export from P compartment and Hh distribution and reception in the A compartment.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Cytonemes from the A and P compartments meet at the A/P boundary in the basal part of the epithelium.
source: Cytoneme-mediated long distant communication between Hh-producing and Hh-responding cells is visualized when Ihog-RFP marked cytonemes from the A and P compartments meet at the A/P boundary in the basal part of the epithelium (Figure 1G, arrow; Video 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G and Video 3.

claim: Anterior compartment cells overexpressing Ihog extend basal cytonemes which invade the P compartment and accumulate Hh.
source: Anterior compartment cells overexpressing Ihog consistently extend basal cytonemes, which invade the P compartment and heavily accumulate Hh (Figure 1H, arrow; Video 4), leadingto an extended Hh gradient (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H, Video 4, and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Ihog overexpression in A compartment cells leads to an extended Hh gradient.
source: Anterior compartment cells overexpressing Ihog consistently extend basal cytonemes, which invade the P compartment and heavily accumulate Hh (Figure 1H, arrow; Video 4), leadingto an extended Hh gradient (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Hh-receiving cells generate dynamic cytonemes directed towards Hh-producing cells.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that Hh-receiving cells generate dynamic cytonemes directed towards Hh-producing cells, and that these A cytonemes can influence the graded distribution of Hh.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: A cytonemes can influence the graded distribution of Hh.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that Hh-receiving cells generate dynamic cytonemes directed towards Hh-producing cells, and that these A cytonemes can influence the graded distribution of Hh.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: In shiK44A mutant background, Hh co-localizes with Ptc at the basal membrane of Hh-receiving cells.
source: In this mutant background, Hh co-localizes with Ptc at the basal membrane of Hh-receiving cells, revealing the presence of filopodia-like structures oriented in the A-P axis (Figure 2A, arrowheads).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Extracellular staining of Ptc and Hh confirms basal localization of Hh-Ptc complex for signal reception.
source: Extracellular staining of Ptc and Hh confirms this basal localization of Hh-Ptc complex for signal reception (Figure 2A', arrow).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A'.

claim: Cytonemes from Hh-producing cells invade the A compartment to contact the basal membrane of the Hh reception region in A cells.
source: Furthermore, cytonemes from Hh-producing cells (labelled with Ihog-RFP) invade the A compartment to contact the basal membrane of the Hh reception region (labelled with Ptc) in A cells (Figure 2B arrowheads and 2B' arrow).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and 2B'.

claim: The receptor Ptc is localized in A cytonemes when its internalization is impeded in the Hh-receiving cells.
source: We can also detect the receptor Ptc localized in A cytonemes when its internalization is impeded in the Hh-receiving cells (Figure 2C and C', arrow) or co-localizing with P compartment Ihog-RFP labelled cytonemes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C, C', and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: A compartment cells receive the Hh signal through their cytonemes, which also contain Ptc.
source: These results indicate that A compartment cells receive the Hh signal through their cytonemes, which also contain Ptc.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Hh-CD2 protein localizes to basal cytonemes.
source: As expected Hh-CD2 localizes to basal cytonemes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), since this form of Hh is permanently anchored to the plasma membranes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Hh-CD2 protein expression allows visualization of interactions between cytonemes emanating from the A compartment and cytonemes from the P compartment along their lengths.
source: Therefore, the Hh-CD2 protein expression allowed us to visualize interactions between cytonemes emanating from the A compartment (expressing Ihog-RFP) and cytonemes from the P compartment (expressing Hh-CD2) along their lengths (Figure 3A, arrowheads; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Hh-receiving cytonemes accumulate the co-receptor Ihog at contact sites with Hh-CD2-presenting cytonemes.
source: Hh-receiving cytonemes accumulate the co-receptor Ihog at contact sites with Hh-CD2-presenting cytonemes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and C', compare C with D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and C'.

claim: The Hh receptor Ptc is localized in contact sites between cytonemes from A and P compartment cells.
source: Noticeably, the Hh receptor Ptc is also localized in these contact sites between cytonemes from A and P compartment cells (Figure 3B, arrows; Figure 3—figure supplement 1C' and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C' and E.

claim: The Hh receptor complex binds Hh-CD2 protein at the basal membrane of Hh signal-receiving cytonemes.
source: These results suggest that the Hh receptor complex binds Hh-CD2 protein at the basal membrane of Hh signal-receiving cytonemes, while blockage in Hh release and internalization results in Ptc also being retained in the cytoneme membrane (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, compare E with F).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: Hh reception is mediated by contacts between Hh-sending and Hh-receiving cytonemes.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that Hh reception is mediated by contacts between Hh-sending and Hh-receiving cytonemes.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Heparan sulphate proteoglycans (HSPGs) are key players in cell-matrix interaction, cell-cell signalling, and long-range Hh function.
source: Heparan sulphate proteoglycans (HSPGs) are key players in cell-matrix interaction, cell-cell signalling, and long-range Hh function (Lin, 2004; Tabata and Takei, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: P compartment cytonemes do not normally extend along mutant HSPG clones located at the A/P compartment border.
source: We have previously demonstrated that P compartment cytonemes do not normally extend along mutant HSPG clones located at the A/P compartment border (Bischoff et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: The Drosophila glypicans Dally and Dlp are required for both Hh presentation and reception.
source: The Drosophila glypicans Dally and Dlp are required for both Hh presentation and reception (Ayers et al., 2010; Bilioni et al., 2013; Han et al., 2004a; Yan et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: Extension of Ihog-RFP expressing cytonemes is significantly reduced when glypicans levels are lowered by knocking down Dally or Dlp in the opposite compartment.
source: We observe that extension of Ihog-RFP expressing cytonemes is significantly reduced when glypicans levels are lowered by knocking down Dally or Dlp, in the opposite compartment (Figure 7A–C, arrows; Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–D, arrows).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A-C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: Cytonemes are rarely detected crossing through dally and dlp double mutant clones.
source: In agreement with this observation, cytonemes are rarely detected crossing through dally and dlp double mutant clones (Figure 7D, arrowhead).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Cytonemes emanating from the A compartment cells accumulate Dally and Dlp present in the neighbouring P compartment cells.
source: In addition, cytonemes emanating from the A compartment cells accumulate Dally and Dlp present in the neighbouring P compartment cells (Figure 7E, arrow; Bilioni et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E and citation to previous work.

claim: Glypicans are required for cytoneme spreading.
source: In summary, all these results demonstrate the requirement of glypicans for cytoneme spreading and their specific role in the cytoneme-mediated interplay between Hh-producing and Hh-receiving cells.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Glypicans have a specific role in the cytoneme-mediated interplay between Hh-producing and Hh-receiving cells.
source: In summary, all these results demonstrate the requirement of glypicans for cytoneme spreading and their specific role in the cytoneme-mediated interplay between Hh-producing and Hh-receiving cells.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Ihog and glypicans accumulate along the membranes of the Hh-sending and Hh-receiving interacting cytonemes when Ihog is overexpressed in one compartment and either Dally or Dlp overexpressed in the other one.
source: We then analysed the interaction between confronting cytonemes at the A/P compartment border when Ihog is overexpressed in one compartment and either Dally or Dlp overexpressed in the other one. Remarkably, we observe an accumulation of Ihog and glypicans along the membranes of the Hh-sending and Hh-receiving interacting cytonemes (Figure 8A–D, arrowheads).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A-D.

claim: Contact sites between Hh-sending and Hh-receiving cytonemes present well-defined annular structures containing both Ihog and the glypicans Dally and Dlp.
source: Moreover, these contact sites present well-defined annular structures containing both Ihog and the glypicans Dally and Dlp (Figure 8A' and B', arrows) similar to the ones visualized by GRASP (Figure 4D and E, arrows).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A', B', and comparison with Figure 4D and E.

claim: Hh-sending and Hh-receiving cytonemes touch-contact along their lengths.
source: These results show again that Hh-sending and Hh-receiving cytonemes touch-contact along their lengths and, importantly, reveal a role for an Ihog/glypican interaction in trans during this cell-cell interface.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Ihog/glypican interaction in trans plays a role during cell-cell interface between Hh-sending and Hh-receiving cytonemes.
source: These results show again that Hh-sending and Hh-receiving cytonemes touch-contact along their lengths and, importantly, reveal a role for an Ihog/glypican interaction in trans during this cell-cell interface.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Both A and P compartment cytonemes weigh in the formation of the Hh gradient.
source: Here we have extended this work and showed that the cytonemes emanating from signal-receiving cells in the A compartment also have a critical role in Hh gradient formation. Therefore, both A and P compartment cytonemes weigh in the formation of the Hh gradient.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The two sets of cytonemes make contact through the basal side of the epithelium.
source: The two sets of cytonemes make contact through the basal side of the epithelium and show similar values of average maximum extent, lifetime, and elongation and retraction velocities.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A and P cytonemes contact predominantly on the anterior side of the compartment boundary.
source: A and P cytonemes contact predominantly on the anterior side of the compartment boundary.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data, particularly GRASP experiments.

claim: Receiving cytonemes include components of the Hh reception complex (Ptc, Ihog, Dlp and Dally).
source: Furthermore, receiving cytonemes include components of the Hh reception complex (Ptc, Ihog, Dlp and Dally), supporting their signalling role; consistently, we find that manipulating their actin dynamics modifies Hh graded signalling.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing localization of these components in cytonemes.

claim: Manipulating actin dynamics of receiving cytonemes modifies Hh graded signalling.
source: Furthermore, receiving cytonemes include components of the Hh reception complex (Ptc, Ihog, Dlp and Dally), supporting their signalling role; consistently, we find that manipulating their actin dynamics modifies Hh graded signalling.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Signal transmission might be dependent on cytoneme stability and the frequency with which A and P cytonemes make contact.
source: As implied in our earlier study, signal transmission might be dependent on cytoneme stability and the frequency with which A and P cytonemes make contact.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the data and previous work.

claim: More Hh would be delivered to A cells close to the A/P compartment border than to those further from the signal source.
source: More Hh would be delivered to A cells close to the A/P compartment border than to those further from the signal source.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the cytoneme contact model.

claim: A cytonemes from cells close to the A/P boundary establish contact primarily with the cytonemes from adjacent P compartment cells.
source: In agreement with this hypothesis, GRASP fluorescence analysis suggests that A cytonemes from cells close to the A/P boundary establish contact primarily with the cytonemes from adjacent P compartment cells, where Hh would also be delivered by further P cells cytonemes.
evidence: This is an inference based on GRASP fluorescence analysis.

claim: The sum of spatial interactions between cytonemes would result in high levels of Hh signalling close to the A/P border.
source: The sum of these spatial interactions would then result in high levels of Hh signalling close to the A/P border.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the proposed model.

claim: The longest cytonemes from cells further from the A/P compartment border would interconnect to deliver the reduced levels of Hh signalling in more distant A cells.
source: The longest cytonemes from cells further from the A/P compartment border would interconnect to deliver the reduced levels of Hh signalling in more distant A cells.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the proposed model.

claim: Membrane-tethered Hh (Hh-CD2) results in a non graded signalling response.
source: Interestingly, the expression in the P compartment of membrane-tethered Hh (Hh-CD2), which results in a non graded signalling response (Strigini and Cohen, 1997), alters the receiving cytonemes cargo by hindering Ptc internalization.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Strigini and Cohen, 1997.

claim: Hh-CD2 expression alters the receiving cytonemes cargo by hindering Ptc internalization.
source: Interestingly, the expression in the P compartment of membrane-tethered Hh (Hh-CD2), which results in a non graded signalling response (Strigini and Cohen, 1997), alters the receiving cytonemes cargo by hindering Ptc internalization.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both Ptc and Ihog accumulate in A compartment cytonemes at contact sites with Hh-CD2 expressing P compartment cytonemes.
source: Despite that Hh receptor Ptc is usually rapidly internalized and not visualized at the plasma membrane, both Ptc and Ihog accumulate in A compartment cytonemes at contact sites with Hh-CD2 expressing P compartment cytonemes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Hh release from the presenting membranes is necessary for proper signaling.
source: Thus, this form of Hh attached to membranes plausibly affects the reception process, potentially explaining the absence of a signalling gradient and further confirming that Hh release from the presenting membranes is necessary.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Hh-CD2 experimental results.

claim: Proteolytic removal of both lipidated peptides releases active Sonic hedgehog (Shh) from the surface of cultured cells.
source: However, in strong support of a Hh shedding process, proteolytic removal of both lipidated peptides releases active Sonic hedgehog (Shh) from the surface of cultured cells (Ohlig et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ohlig et al., 2011.

claim: Ihog trans interaction with glypicans in cytoneme-mediated cell-cell contacts has a critical role for cytoneme dynamics.
source: On the other hand, Ihog trans interaction with glypicans in cytoneme-mediated cell-cell contacts has a critical role for cytoneme dynamics.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The spreading capacity of Ihog overexpressing cytonemes is dependent on the glypicans presence in the membranes of neighbouring cells.
source: The spreading capacity of Ihog overexpressing cytonemes is dependent on the glypicans presence in the membranes of neighbouring cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cytonemes protruding from one compartment aberrantly extend over the other compartment when it is mutant for dally and dlp.
source: Cytonemes protruding from one compartment aberrantly extend over the other compartment when is mutant for dally and dlp.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Tout-velu (Ttv) and Brother of Ttv (Btv) proteins are required to stabilize Ihog cytonemes.
source: This is in agreement with our previous results showing that the Tout-velu (Ttv) and Brother of Ttv (Btv) proteins (needed for the HSPGs synthesis) are required to stabilize Ihog cytonemes (Bischoff et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Dally or Dlp overexpressing cytonemes from one compartment are stabilized by Ihog overexpressing cytonemes from the other one.
source: In addition, Dally or Dlp overexpressing cytonemes from one compartment seem to be stabilized by Ihog overexpressing cytonemes from the other one, with which they associate along their length by trans interaction between Ihog and glypicans.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cytonemes from one compartment can contribute to the stability of the cytonemes from the other one with which they contact.
source: Thus, cytonemes from one compartment can contribute to the stability of the cytonemes from the other one with which they contact.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Dynamic interactions between A and P compartment cytonemes play an important role in the formation of the Hh gradient.
source: Taken together, these results establish that dynamic interactions between A and P compartment cytonemes play an important role in the formation of the Hh gradient.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Components for both reception and presentation of Hh critically influence the performance of cytoneme interaction.
source: In conjunction components for both reception and presentation of Hh critically influence the performance of this cytoneme interaction.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: A and P compartment cytonemes overlap in a region spanning the A/P compartment boundary.
source: The membrane-bound GRASP fluorescence shows that A and P compartment cytonemes overlap in a region spanning the A/P compartment boundary.
evidence: This is supported by GRASP experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Direct 'kissing' contacts appear along the membranes of interacting A and P cytonemes to connect the two sets of cytonemes.
source: Within this region, direct 'kissing' contacts appear along the membranes of interacting A and P cytonemes to connect the two sets of cytonemes.
evidence: This is supported by GRASP experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Contact points between cytonemes are associated with annular structures, which may represent more stable links.
source: These contact points are associated with annular structures, which may represent more stable links and are reminiscent of synaptic buttons.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental observations.

claim: Similar 'synaptic contacts' have been previously described between air sac primordium (ASP) and wing disc cells for Dpp morphogen transference.
source: Similar 'synaptic contacts' have been previously described between air sac primordium (ASP) and wing disc cells for Dpp morphogen transference (Roy et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Roy et al., 2014.

claim: ASP cells receive Dpp by emitting long cytonemes that contact with the target cell of the wing disc by their tips.
source: ASP cells receive Dpp by emitting long cytonemes that contact with the target cell of the wing disc by their tips.
evidence: This is knowledge from cited work (Roy et al., 2014).

claim: Dpp uses a cytoneme-mediated contact-dependent mechanism for signalling at distance.
source: Although Dpp uses a cytoneme-mediated contact-dependent mechanism for signalling at distance, the reception takes place where Dpp-receiving cytoneme tip contacts with the Dpp source cell body, in contrast with the cytoneme-cytoneme contacts here described for Hh.
evidence: This is knowledge from cited work and comparison with current findings.

claim: Hh moves along cytonemes in multivesicular bodies (MVB) to be secreted as extracellular vesicles known as exosomes.
source: We have previously demonstrated that Hh moves along cytonemes in multivesicular bodies (MVB) to be secreted as extracellular vesicles known as exosomes (Gradilla et al., 2014), which raises intriguing questions about the mechanism of interaction between exosomal Hh and its receptor Ptc in the A cytonemes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Ptc and Hh can be detected co-localizing with cytoneme contact sites.
source: Interestingly, Ptc and Hh can be detected co-localizing with cytoneme contact sites, suggesting that they could represent specific sites for Hh reception and internalization.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cytoneme contact sites could represent specific sites for Hh reception and internalization.
source: Interestingly, Ptc and Hh can be detected co-localizing with cytoneme contact sites, suggesting that they could represent specific sites for Hh reception and internalization.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on experimental observations.

claim: Hh containing exosomes could be received at intimate contacts between P and A cytonemes.
source: These data strengthen our proposal of cytoneme-mediated Hh morphogen distribution and suggest that Hh containing exosomes could be received at intimate contacts between P and A cytonemes.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the data presented.

claim: Cytonemes are able to cross ptc−/− and smo−/− clones, enabling the Hh transport from P to A cells for Hh signalling reestablishment in wild type cells located anterior to the clones.
source: Finally, we have shown that cytonemes are able to cross ptc−/− and smo−/− clones, enabling the Hh transport from P to A cells for Hh signalling reestablishment in wild type cells located anterior to the clones.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The Hh signal can cross small mutant clones of ptc and smo to reach the adjacent wild type territory.
source: In agreement, it is known that the Hh signal can cross small mutant clones of ptc and smo to reach the adjacent wild type territory.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Similar behaviour has been described for ptc−/− or smo−/− clones induced in the A abdominal histoblast nests and attributed to different cell polarity and cell affinity.
source: Similar behaviour, has been described for ptc−/− or smo−/− clones induced in the A abdominal histoblast nests and attributed to different cell polarity and cell affinity (Struhl et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Struhl et al., 1997.

claim: Hh transport and reception by cytoneme-mediated cell-cell contacts can explain the Hh signalling in wild type cells located anterior to ptc−/− and smo−/− clones.
source: Therefore, Hh transport and reception by cytoneme-mediated cell-cell contacts can explain the Hh signalling in wild type cells located anterior to ptc−/− and smo−/− clones.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The described intimate interaction between P and A cytonemes at membrane contact sites may facilitate morphogen reception.
source: The described intimate interaction between these two sets of cytonemes at membrane contact sites, where ligand and receptor complex colocalize, may facilitate morphogen reception.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the data presented.

claim: Clones of ptc−/− and smo−/− located at the A/P compartment border are unable to internalize Hh, but do not block Hh signal transmission to more anterior wild type cells.
source: It has been previously described that clones of ptc−/− and smo−/− located at the A/P compartment border are unable to internalize Hh, but do not block Hh signal transmission to more anterior wild type cells (Chen and Struhl, 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Chen and Struhl, 1996.

claim: Hh could be transported across mutant ptc−/− and smo−/− clones in cytonemes that act as conveyer belts for long distance transport.
source: Our cytoneme transport hypothesis predicts that Hh could be transported across mutant ptc−/− and smo−/− clones in cytonemes that act as conveyer belts for long distance transport.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the cytoneme transport model.

claim: Hh-producing cells still spread cytonemes when Hh reception was prevented in the A compartment by knocking down either Ptc or Smo, or both co-receptors Ihog and Boi.
source: Accordingly, we observed that Hh-producing cells still spread cytonemes when Hh reception was prevented in the A compartment by knocking down either Ptc or Smo, or both co-receptors Ihog and Brother of Ihog (Boi) at the same time (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cytonemes from both compartments were still formed upon the elimination of Hh using the hh thermosensitive allele (hhts2).
source: In addition, cytonemes from both compartments were still formed upon the elimination of Hh (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–F) using the hh thermosensitive allele (hhts2) (Ma et al., 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-F and citation to Ma et al., 1993.

claim: No apparent changes in Hh-receiving cytonemes were observed when Hh reception was prevented in ptc−/− MARCM clones expressing Ihog-YFP.
source: No apparent changes in Hh-receiving cytonemes were also observed when Hh reception was prevented in ptc−/− MARCM clones expressing Ihog-YFP (Figure 5—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2G.

claim: The presence of the network of cytonemes is independent of Hh signaling.
source: Therefore, the presence of the network of cytonemes is independent of Hh signaling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing cytoneme formation in the absence of Hh signaling.

claim: Hh signalling is fully activated in ptc−/− mutant clones due to the lack of normal Ptc repression upon Smo.
source: Hh signalling is fully activated in ptc−/− mutant clones due to the lack of normal Ptc repression upon Smo (Chen and Struhl, 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Chen and Struhl, 1996.

claim: Hh protein can be detected in the wild type cells anterior to the ptc−/− mutant clone.
source: We show here that Hh protein can be detected in the wild type cells anterior to the ptc−/− mutant clone (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Cytonemes emanating from Hh-producing cells orient normally towards the A compartment cells across a ptc mutant clone induced adjacent to the A/P border in the wing disc.
source: Accordingly, with previous experiments (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), cytonemes emanating from Hh-producing cells orient normally towards the A compartment cells across a ptc mutant clone induced adjacent to the A/P border in the wing disc (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Abdominal histoblasts of the P compartment produce cytonemes that cross a ptc−/− clone in their way towards the anterior cells.
source: Consistently, abdominal histoblasts of the P compartment produce cytonemes that cross a ptc−/− clone in their way towards the anterior cells (Figure 5C, Video 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and Video 6.

claim: Cytonemes have similar dynamics (maximum extent, lifetime and elongation and retraction velocities) when crossing wild type or ptc−/− mutant territories.
source: These cytonemes have similar dynamics (maximum extent, lifetime and elongation and retraction velocities) when crossing wild type or ptc−/− mutant territories (Figure 5C and C', Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5C, C' and Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Cytoneme dynamics is independent of the presence of the receptor Ptc.
source: Therefore, cytoneme dynamics is independent of the presence of the receptor Ptc.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing similar cytoneme dynamics in wild type and ptc mutant territories.

claim: GRASP signal indicates that cytonemes from the Hh-receiving cells reach the Hh-sending cytonemes close to the A/P compartment border.
source: In addition, GRASP signal indicates that cytonemes from the Hh-receiving cells reach the Hh-sending cytonemes close to the A/P compartment border (Figure 5D, region 1 arrowhead).
evidence: This claim is supported by GRASP experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: GRASP signal is detected along A cytonemes that cross ptc−/− clones and interact with the P compartment cytonemes.
source: So that, GRASP signal is detected along these A cytonemes that cross the clone and interact with the P compartment cytonemes (Figure 5E, arrows).
evidence: This claim is supported by GRASP experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: In subapical regions of the epithelium, where cytonemes are too short to reach the P compartment, GRASP fluorescence is not detected.
source: However, in subapical regions of the epithelium, where cytonemes are too short to reach the P compartment, GRASP fluorescence is not detected (Figure 5D, asterisk).
evidence: This claim is supported by GRASP experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: When a ptc−/− clone is too large, wild type anterior cells are not able to respond to Hh.
source: It is also known that when a ptc−/− clone is too large, wild type anterior cells are not able to respond to Hh (Chen and Struhl, 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Chen and Struhl, 1996.

claim: When a ptc−/− clone is too large, cytonemes extending from the A cells do not reach the P cells and no GRASP fluorescence is detected.
source: Noticeably, in this situation we observe that cytonemes extending from the A cells do not reach the P cells and no GRASP fluorescence is detected (Figure 5D, region 2 arrowhead).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: In smo−/− clones originating in the A compartment, the A/P compartment border is re-established in the position where Hh signalling is activated in cells anterior to the clone.
source: In smo−/− clones originating in the A compartment, and monitored by low levels of Ci expression, the A/P compartment border is re-established in the position where Hh signalling is activated in cells anterior to the clone (Blair and Ralston, 1997; Rodriguez and Basler, 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Blair and Ralston, 1997 and Rodriguez and Basler, 1997.

claim: A compartment smo−/− cells integrate into the P compartment and maintain a straight boundary at the nearest anterior cells where Hh is then received.
source: As a result, A compartment smo−/− cells integrate into the P compartment and maintain a straight boundary at the nearest anterior cells where Hh is then received.
evidence: This is an inference based on cited work about smo mutant clone behavior.

claim: Hh visualized within smo−/− clones is restricted to the most basal region of epithelial cells.
source: The Hh visualized within smo−/− clones is restricted to the most basal region of epithelial cells, demonstrating again that Hh travels mostly basally (Figure 6A, arrowhead) (Bilioni et al., 2013; Bischoff et al., 2013; Callejo et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A and citations to previous work.

claim: Hh travels mostly basally in the epithelium.
source: The Hh visualized within smo−/− clones is restricted to the most basal region of epithelial cells, demonstrating again that Hh travels mostly basally (Figure 6A, arrowhead) (Bilioni et al., 2013; Bischoff et al., 2013; Callejo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and cited previous work.

claim: Cytonemes emanating from cells anterior to smo−/− clones are loaded with Hh.
source: In addition, cytonemes emanating from cells anterior to the clone are loaded with Hh (Figure 6B, arrowhead), and P cytonemes cross a smo−/− clone reaching the A/P compartment border (Figure 6C, arrow).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: P cytonemes cross a smo−/− clone reaching the A/P compartment border.
source: In addition, cytonemes emanating from cells anterior to the clone are loaded with Hh (Figure 6B, arrowhead), and P cytonemes cross a smo−/− clone reaching the A/P compartment border (Figure 6C, arrow).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: GRASP fluorescence is detected where the compartment border is re-established anterior to a smo−/− clone.
source: Accordingly, GRASP fluorescence is detected where the compartment border is re-established anterior to a smo−/− clone (Figure 6D, arrow).
evidence: This claim is supported by GRASP experimental data shown in Figure 6D.
